subject: general
question: Which committee is constituted by the Government if population of a particular area exceeds 3 lakh?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ward Committee**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Under Article 243S of the Constitution of India, a **Ward Committee** must be constituted in municipalities with a population exceeding 3 lakh. 
 
• Constitution (Seventy Fourth Amendment) Act, 1992 has introduced a new Part IXA in the Constitution, which deals with Municipalities in an article 243 P to 243 ZG. 
 
• This amendment, also known as Nagarpalika Act, came into force on 1st June 1993.
 
• It has given constitutional status to the municipalities and brought them under the justifiable part of the constitution.
 
• States were put under constitutional obligation to adopt municipalities as per the system enshrined in the constitution.
 
• Under clause (1) of article 243S, it has been provided that there shall be constituted Wards Committees, consisting of one or more wards, within the territorial area of a Municipality having a population of three lacs or more.
 
• A ward is an area in a metro or local municipality, which has clearly defined boundaries.
 
• A ward committee is a democratically elected body that represents a wide variety of community interests and meets regularly under the chairperson who is the ward councilor.
 
• Thus, we can say that the minimum population of a municipality to constitute ward committees should be 3 lakhs or above.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Nagar Committee**

 
 
• A Nagar Committee, **often referred to as a Nagar Panchayat**, is a local government body for a transitional area—an area in transition from rural to urban.
 
• **It governs smaller towns with a population typically between 20,000 and 100,000.**
 
• Nagar Panchayats are part of the **three-tier structure of local governance under the 74th Amendment,**
 
 

 
• **Metropolitan Committee**

 
 
• The Metropolitan Planning Committee (MPC) is **constituted for planning and coordinating development in metropolitan area**s, which are defined as areas having a population of over 10 lakhs.
 
• This **committee ensures regional planning and resource management** across a larger urban expanse, involving multiple municipalities.
 
• It’s primarily **focused on the metropolitan regions r**ather than smaller urban areas with just 3 lakh population.
 
 
 
• ** District Planning Committee**
 
 
• The District Planning Committee (DPC) is c**onstituted under Article 243ZD of the Constitution.**
 
• It **consolidates plans from Panchayats and municipalities **at the district level and integrates them into a comprehensive development plan for the entire district.
 
• The f**ocus is on overall district-level development,** not just urban areas.
